# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart beats faster than usual when she plays, which is something to monitor.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues sometimes, managed with diet and hydration changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when running around or playing actively, and has a different posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear once, which was treated and hasn't recurred since then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision slightly, but she's learned to adapt.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's tooth enamel is weak, and she requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter than average fingers and stands and walks with a noticeably different posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and prevent further problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage symptoms
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise
* Manage constipation issues through diet and hydration changes

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son complains that things look blurry sometimes. It's been an ongoing issue, and we're concerned it might affect his learning at school. We've tried getting him to wear glasses‚ but he doesn't like them. The blurriness seems to happen more often when he's tired or after playing video games.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes‚ there's fluid in his ear. Doctors have looked at it‚ and they say it's not causing any permanent damage yet‚ but we need to monitor it closely. Sometimes he pulls at his ear when it bothers him‚ especially during flights or when he has a cold.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth break or chip easily. Even when he eats normal foods like apples or carrots‚ we find bits of tooth in his food. We're teaching him how to chew carefully and encouraging him to visit the dentist regularly for check-ups.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's a septal defect that was diagnosed early on. We see specialists regularly for monitoring‚ and they say everything looks stable for now. However‚ we do worry about how this will impact him in sports or when he grows older.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ our boy falls more often than other children. Not just when running around‚ even on flat ground‚ he trips over nothing and scrapes his knee. We watch him closely‚ especially on playgrounds‚ to make sure he doesn't hurt himself badly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Mealtimes are often a struggle. He can get constipated if he doesn't drink enough water‚ and then has trouble passing stool. Some foods also seem to disagree with him‚ giving him bad diarrhea. We try to manage this with diet and making sure he drinks plenty throughout the day.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: One thing that worries us is his struggle with clarity when trying to talk. Sometimes we can't understand what he says‚ and he gets frustrated because we keep asking him to repeat himself. Speech therapy has helped a lot‚ but it's still something we work on daily.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a diagnosed septal defect in her heart, which is being monitored and managed by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky about food and will often refuse to eat certain things, leading to challenges at mealtimes in ensuring she gets a balanced diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted rather quickly when engaging in physical activities, and even simple play can leave her feeling drained after a short while.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond immediately when called, appearing distracted or not paying attention, which can be concerning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes when trying to focus on something, especially when watching TV or playing with toys, as her eyes seem to get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and tends to avoid eating meats or crunchy vegetables because they're difficult for her to chew.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers on one hand, which is being monitored for its effect on her development and dexterity over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the septal defect.
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in her heart, which requires regular monitoring to ensure it doesn't affect her daily life too much.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky with food and often refuses certain meals, although it's not a major concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, which are managed effectively with her neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and turns the TV volume up really high to hear her favorite shows.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class, even when sitting close, and often squints or leans forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weaker than average tooth enamel, and regular dental check-ups are necessary to take better care of her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, although some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which requires ongoing monitoring and management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weaker than average tooth enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor the patient's vision problems
* Regular monitoring of the patient's heart condition to ensure it doesn't affect her daily life too much
* Ongoing management and monitoring of the patient's epileptic seizures
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor the patient's scoliosis
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and management of her conditions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a younger child, including trouble latching on and getting frustrated easily, although this has improved over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient lacks coordination and balance compared to her peers, falls more often, and has delayed speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions when spoken to, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the television or when reading books, suggesting potential eyesight issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require frequent dental visits due to issues like cavities and weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech and may require additional support in educational settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has subtle differences in movement and walking compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to detect and manage potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart condition.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart problem with a hole in it, requiring multiple doctor visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, eats little, and does not gain weight like other babies.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient walks and sits late, takes more time than other kids, and has developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear once and has hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (can see close things better than things far away).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing and can only eat soft food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient talks funny and people don't understand her, and has developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's back curves.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers and curved 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups
* Regular hearing reviews
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG)
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull)
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy may be beneficial

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, and is working on correcting it with glasses and exercises.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue more quickly during physical activities, suggesting potential heart health issues.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits a strong feeding aversion to several food types, leading to challenges in introducing new foods and concerns about nutrient deficiency.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated than others his age, with delays in mastering simple tasks like tying shoelaces or riding a bike, and shows slightly underdeveloped balance and movement skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has instances where he doesn't seem to hear his name being called, even when in the same room, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often complains about struggling to see the board during lessons at school, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth can be quite brittle, breaking or chipping easily, requiring extra care with dental hygiene and regular dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may impact his learning, and he may require additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or require Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue during physical activity and has difficulty keeping up with peers, suggesting potential cardiac issues. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures, showing sensitivity to certain smells and textures, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, which are managed with medication and close monitoring by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes when trying to focus, suggesting vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring dental repairs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, emphasizing the importance of regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture and delayed fontanelle closure, with the soft palate not closing properly during speech or swallowing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly), curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased risk of scoliosis or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Hearing reviews up to age 5 to detect and manage potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.
* Regular monitoring and management of epileptic seizures.
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.

Parent: His teeth aren't as strong as they should be; the dentist mentioned something about weak enamel, and we're having to be super careful about what he eats and making sure he brushes them properly.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: He has these... episodes, where he just stares off into space. They're really frightening, to be honest. It's like he's not even there for a few seconds, and then he snaps back. I don't know what causes them or how to help him when they happen.

Parent: Well, there are these undescended testicles... and hip dysplasia was diagnosed recently. The doctors are keeping an eye on both, especially since they could potentially cause more problems if not addressed properly.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than other kids her age, especially when playing or running around with friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with her food and tends to avoid certain types of food, but it's not due to digestion issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which is managed closely with her doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks people to repeat themselves because she didn't quite catch what they said the first time, indicating some hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and uses glasses to help with seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods and tends to avoid those types of food or takes smaller bites to manage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any concerns.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and is selective about food, making mealtime stressful, and there are challenges in encouraging her to try new foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding. There is also a lack of interest in feeding that can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits clumsiness, lack of coordination, and seems less balanced than peers, indicating potential neurological issues affecting motor skills and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking for repetitions of what was said, especially in noisy environments, and squints, which can affect focus and learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which can make it hard for her to focus on things directly in front of her, potentially affecting learning and daily activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with tooth decay and weakness, necessitating more frequent dental visits than typical for her age group.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended, with some requiring specialist SEN dental care due to significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's squinting and hearing difficulties may impact her ability to focus and learn in a traditional classroom setting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's feeding difficulties and selectivity may contribute to behavioral challenges, and her clumsiness could affect her participation in certain activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves slightly differently than her peers, though not drastically so, indicating potential skeletal or motor skill issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, potentially leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address tooth decay and weakness.
* Hearing reviews to age 5, even if earlier reviews indicate clear responses, to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis, to assess for heart conditions.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to monitor for skeletal anomalies.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental and behavioral challenges.
* Monitor growth velocity, and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile, taking into account familial heights.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a known valve abnormality in his heart, which is monitored regularly with check-ups and consultations with his cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had poor feeding in infancy, but this seems to have resolved itself as he grew older.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other children his age, as if he loses balance easier or doesn't judge distances well. He also moves a bit differently compared to his peers, almost as if he's still learning how to coordinate his movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, and some may have developmental delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up very high, even when reminded it's already loud enough, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters, and squints a lot, leaning forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods or drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking, which can be quite pronounced at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a different posture and movement coordination compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review to monitor the known valve abnormality
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and coordination issues
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue, the specifics of which are not fully understood by the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not gaining weight as quickly as other kids, which is a concern that needs to be monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age, which could indicate a neurological issue, and has developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and there is a wide range of developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing when the TV isn't loud enough and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints a lot when looking at things, indicating a potential vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip really easily, indicating weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind in development compared to other children, which may impact educational needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many attend mainstream primary school but may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and falls more often than other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer to close than it should have.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent enamel issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart valve issue.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and behavioural differences.

Parent: Well, we've noticed he seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly. For instance, if we're watching TV together, he'll respond to loud noises but sometimes doesn't react to softer voices or certain tones. It's like he's picking and choosing what he wants to listen to, but I'm not sure if that's normal or not.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: He's been complaining about tooth sensitivity lately, especially when he eats cold food like ice cream or cold drinks. He says it hurts and makes him jump. We've tried using special toothpaste, but it doesn't seem to make much difference.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... the doctors found a septal defect. They said it's a hole in the heart that didn't close properly after birth. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it and make sure it doesn't cause more serious problems. It's been a worry for us since the diagnosis.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has these episodes where he just stares off into space. It's like he's in a trance or something. We call them his 'blank spells'. They can happen anytime - during play, while eating... it's really frightening because we never know when they'll happen. And sometimes he gets rigid and unresponsive for a few seconds before snapping back to reality.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been an issue for him. He struggles to go to the bathroom regularly and when he does, it's often very painful for him. We've tried changing his diet and encouraging more fluid intake but nothing seems to work consistently.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: There are two main things. Firstly, the delayed fontanelle closure has been a concern since birth. The doctors have been monitoring it closely to ensure it doesn't lead to further complications. Secondly, he struggles with clarity when trying to talk. His words aren't always clear, and he gets frustrated when we can't understand him. It's heartbreaking to see him try so hard to communicate but not being able to express himself properly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes I call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's like he's not hearing me or maybe just ignoring me? But if I go over to him and say it again، he'll usually answer. I don't know if it's his hearing or just him being a bit distracted.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are a worry for me because the dentist said the enamel is weak. We have to be super careful with sugary foods and make sure he brushes them really well to prevent cavities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When he plays outside with friends， his breathing gets much faster than the other kids. Even when they're all running around together， my son seems to be panting more. I've mentioned it to his dad， but we haven't done anything about it yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Poor baby... he has low muscle tone. The physiotherapist is working with him to improve it. You can see it when he walks or tries to hold things; it's just a bit more effortful for him than for other kids his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Eating can be tricky sometimes. He's super fussy about food textures and won't eat certain things because of how they feel in his mouth. Like， mashed potatoes are okay but not if they're lumpy at all.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... his fingers are shorter than usual. We were told it's just something he was born with and doesn't affect anything else.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing and panting, especially when engaging in physical activities like playing outside with friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than his peers when they are all engaging in the same physical activity, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods due to their texture, indicating potential feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has low muscle tone, which is evident when he walks or tries to hold things, requiring more effort than his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes does not respond immediately when called, suggesting potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV and has difficulty reading books unless he is close to them, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, requiring careful brushing and a diet low in sugary foods to prevent cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often exhibit behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, which may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual, a characteristic common in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, delayed closure of the soft spot on the head, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak enamel
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart conditions
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify potential skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks to have things repeated when spoken to, indicating possible hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or when reading books, indicating possible vision problems.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual, and there was an issue with the fontanelle not closing properly after birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets really fast when playing, which may indicate a potential heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, with certain food textures causing upset and making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy, tripping over her own feet or having trouble walking straight, which may indicate neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks for things to be repeated because she didn't understand them the first time, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, with a potential diagnosis of hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem a bit weak, especially the enamel, requiring regular brushing and dental visits.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and has shorter fingers than usual.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Eyesight review to confirm potential hypermetropia and monitor for other vision problems.
* Cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and clumsiness.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups to monitor his health closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movements that are sometimes too loose and other times too hard, and dietary changes are being tried to regulate his bowel habits better.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in people with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally and works closely with his neurologist to manage them and adjust his medication as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to pick up certain sounds without difficulty but struggles with others, and has had issues with hearing that may be related to the development of his ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things appear blurry at times, especially when trying to focus on something far away, and has had his eyes checked with a doctor suggesting it might be related to how his eyes are developing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, and regular brushing and proper dental care are being emphasized to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay and is receiving speech therapy to improve his communication skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, and may experience skeletal anomalies such as scoliosis or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing development.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Consider a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Referral for speech therapy to address speech delay.
* Regular monitoring of bowel habits and adjustment of dietary changes as needed.
* Neurological monitoring and adjustment of medication as needed for seizure management.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired easily, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about what he eats, with certain textures making him refuse to eat altogether.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient trips over his own feet sometimes and is not as good at running around as other kids, which may indicate a neurological issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid in his ear and has trouble seeing things far away, with a diagnosis of myopia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away and has been diagnosed with myopia, for which he is waiting to get glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth hurt when he eats cold things like ice cream.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient doesn't talk as much as he should for his age, which is a concern for his development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing
* Eyesight review to monitor the patient's vision and adjust glasses as needed
* Cardiac review to investigate the patient's heart condition and provide appropriate treatment
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any delays or difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary
* Consideration of a skeletal review to investigate any potential skeletal issues

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: She has this habit of rubbing her eyes, especially when she's trying to focus on something. It's almost like she's straining to see, and it makes her eyes get really red and watery.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Loud noises really overwhelm her. She gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy areas, like malls or playgrounds. Even at home, if the TV is too loud or if her siblings are being too boisterous, she covers her ears and asks us to turn it down.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Cold foods and drinks seem to bother her teeth. She complains of sensitivity whenever she eats something cold, like ice cream or cold water. It's been a recurring issue since her baby teeth started coming in.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When she plays or runs around, her breathing becomes much faster than we expect for a child of her age and activity level. It's noticeable even when she's just playing lightly indoors. We've been meaning to monitor this and possibly discuss it further with our GP.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Coordination seems to be a bit of an issue for her. She trips over her own feet sometimes or has trouble catching a ball because her reactions aren't as quick as they should be for someone her age. 

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtimes can be challenging for her. Some days are better than others, but often she leaves food on her plate or shows little interest in eating certain dishes. This has led to discussions about ensuring she gets enough nutrients.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Her fingers are notably shorter than average, which does cause some difficulty with gripping items like pencils or crayons. Additionally, she was diagnosed with hip dysplasia after a series of checks when she was younger. Both these aspects are under ongoing observation and management by her healthcare team.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when playing or running around, which is noticeable even during light indoor activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing becomes much faster than expected for her age and activity level when playing or running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with mealtimes, showing little interest in eating certain dishes and often leaving food on her plate, which has led to discussions about ensuring she gets enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, tripping over her own feet or having trouble catching a ball due to slow reactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises, covers her ears in crowded or noisy areas, and asks for the volume to be turned down.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a habit of rubbing her eyes, especially when trying to focus, and her eyes get red and watery.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has notably shorter fingers than average, causing difficulty with gripping items, and was diagnosed with hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess bone age and potential skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address coordination issues and developmental delays
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: She seems a bit clumsy and less coordinated than other kids her age when she moves around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures, of varying types, and some may have tethered cord.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: There's fluid in her ear that causes her some discomfort and affects her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She has astigmatism, which sometimes makes it hard for her to see things clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods make her teeth sensitive, and she complains about it often.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: She has hip dysplasia and her posture isn't quite right when she stands or walks - it's noticeable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness.
* Regular hearing reviews to address the fluid in the ear and potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor astigmatism and other vision problems.
* Cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address clumsiness, coordination, and potential developmental delays.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise.
