Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: To be honest, I've noticed he squints a lot. It's like he's having trouble looking straight at things. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He had a glue ear recently. The doctor said it was pretty common in kids his age, but it worried me a bit.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth seem to break or chip really easily. We have to be super careful when he's eating or playing.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's something about his heart valve that the doctors are keeping an eye on. I'm not entirely sure what it means, but they say it's something they need to monitor.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He's got hypotonia. The doctors explained it's a condition that affects his muscle tone. It makes him feel a bit stiffer than other kids.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Oh, food! He's very picky with textures. Some foods he just won't touch because of how they feel. It can be challenging at meal times.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well, there are two main things. First, he's not speaking as much as you'd expect for a child his age. It worries me because all the other kids his age are chatting away. Second, have you seen how he stands and walks? His posture is noticeably different. The way he holds himself just looks a bit off compared to other children.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with food textures, which can make meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, a condition that affects muscle tone, and is not speaking as much as expected for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently and squints.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and large front teeth, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not speaking as much as expected for his age, which may impact his educational development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech development and hypotonia, which may impact his behavior and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable posture differences and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review to monitor heart valve issue
* Speech therapy to address delayed speech development
* Physiotherapy to address hypotonia and posture differences
* Occupational therapy to address feeding difficulties and texture aversions
* Behavioral therapy to address any behavioral differences or anxiety
